svg.text: claudia — front page: moving and copying documents by drag and drop, proposed
Drag a document row onto a place (sidebar, "My places"): it moves there. Hold Ctrl: it is copied — but Claudia asks first, because the document takes its whole history with it.
Drawn on the front page as built (D443). Documents are sealed files (D19, D20): a move is "place the file there, then delete it here", so it needs the owner (E2.10).
A · Drag onto a place: move
The target place is outlined while the pointer is over it. The label says what will happen.

What to settle
Plain drag = move, dropped on a place in "My places". The place is outlined, the label says what happens.
Ctrl while dragging = copy. The label ends in "…" because Claudia asks first (see D).
The move dialog asks for the owner's password every time: deleting the source is owner-only and
passwords belong to each document (D20). Without it a "move" could only ever be a copy.
Live participants are named before the move and returned to the list (as when a document is deleted).
They are not asked: the owner decides, as with deleting.
Feasibility: a page talks only to its own server (D170). A move between places therefore runs shell to
server or server to server (the target pulls the file with a one-time token); the browser alone cannot
relay a sealed file between two origins. To be checked with E3 before this is built.
Copy asks before it acts, as requested. It needs no password: the sealed file is copied as it is.
The copy and the original are independent forks; both show the same past in their history.
The name is sealed into the file (D443), so one place can never hold two of the same name: no "copy
to this place", no "(2)" suffix. A rename-on-copy would re-seal the file: needs the password and a new
kernel operation — not drawn.
Collections stay private bookmarks in the browser. Onto a collection: from a place list it adds, from a
collection view it moves the entry between collections (Ctrl keeps it in the old one too). No question.
A non-owner who drops on a place gets the copy question instead, with the reason ("only the owner
can move it"). Undo: none for the delete on the old place (E2.10); the toast offers "Move it back".
